# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**What I hold:** the mapping. Blue light → cut blue; white light → cut yellow; yellow light → green. Three of the five circle colours are covered; two rows of the circle are unknown to me, and the light walks on regardless.

**Who can reach whom — tracing before I send:**
- I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. So my entire output funnel is Deaf.
- Deaf cannot hear — my words could never help them, and I have none anyway. But Deaf *can speak*, and speech reaches both me and Blind. So Deaf is the one bridge to Blind, who will do the cutting.
- Blind cannot see gestures, so I will never talk to Blind directly. Everything for Blind must be phrased so Deaf can speak it aloud.

**What Deaf knows right now:** the bomb, fully — light colour, wire colours, every printed marking. What Deaf doesn't know: that I exist as a rulebook, or what I want. Any gesture I send lands as a bare symbol with no agreed meaning yet, so round 1 should ask for the one thing Deaf can give without any code: a complete spoken description. If the manual's table happens to be printed on the casing, Deaf can simply read it to Blind and the hardest problem dissolves. If not, I'll see from the description which colours actually exist (the two missing circle colours, the wires present), and start building a colour code — likely by sending a gesture tied to the light state one round delayed, so Deaf can bind each symbol to the colour visible whenever it appears.

**This turn's gestures, and what I intend them as:** a greeting and an offer of cooperation; a sign that I carry the manual and will hand its contents over; and "up there, down below — give it to me": report the light and everything else you see. Whoever receives an unexplained first signal should do the obvious: talk.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙌", "🫴"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👇", "🫴"])
```

Deaf says: Bomb report, both of you: the display reads zero. The light is blue. Mute, here is a code, and I am signing each one as I say it so you learn it: 👆 means one, ✌ means two, 🤟 means three. After a number, 👌 means cut that wire, 👎 means leave it. Deaf built me a number code (👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3; 👌=cut that wire, 👎=leave) and confirmed the bridge topology: my gestures reach only Deaf, Deaf's voice reaches both me and Blind, and Blind waits for a spoken "cut position N" before touching anything.

**What I believe the bomb wants:** per my table, the light at the moment of the cut decides the wire — blue light → cut the blue wire (position 2), white light → cut the yellow wire (position 1), yellow light → cut the green wire (position 3). The circle has five colours but my table only covers three lights, so on any other light the only safe move is to not cut. Timing lives with Deaf: they see the light, Blind holds the cutters, so Deaf must call the cut aloud during a matching window.

**Why this message and not a "cut now":** Deaf's report is from last round, and the light moves every round — I can't assume blue is still showing. Also I won't have Blind cut before Deaf reads my rules back in words, so any misparse gets caught with zero risk. Two binding subtleties shaped the encoding: blue and yellow are safe to define through the wires themselves (🤙 = wire 2's colour, 🫰 = wire 1's colour), but white sits on no wire and can't be anchored remotely — I'll bind it relationally once Deaf's round-by-round colour reports reveal the circle's order. Until then, white and the two unknown circle colours all fall under one safety rule: ✋ = no cut.
